questiontext.text:
Match the systems given in List I with the corresponding surface or bulk phenomena in List II:

List IList II
(a) Water vapours with silica gel(i) Absorption of solvent in the bulk
(b) Water vapours with anhydrous \(\mathrm{CaCl}_2\)(ii) Adsorption on the surface
(c) Methylene blue solution shaken with animal charcoal(iii) Adsorption of coloured dye molecules
(d) Solvent entering the interior of a chalk stick dipped in ink(iv) Absorption throughout the bulk

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In adsorption, the substance concentrates only at the surface of the adsorbent, whereas in absorption, the substance is uniformly distributed throughout the bulk of the solid.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Silica gel dries air because water molecules accumulate on its surface by adsorption, giving (a)-(ii). Anhydrous calcium chloride takes up water vapours uniformly throughout its bulk by absorption, giving (b)-(iv). Animal charcoal removes the colour of methylene blue solution by adsorbing the dye molecules on its surface, giving (c)-(iii). When a chalk stick is dipped in ink, the coloured molecules remain at the surface while the solvent penetrates deeper into the stick by absorption, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Matching types of colloidal systems with examples

questiontext.text:
Match the types of colloidal systems in List I with their respective examples in List II:

List I (Type of colloid)List II (Example)
(a) Solid sol (solid in solid)(i) Whipped cream
(b) Aerosol (liquid in gas)(ii) Gem stones
(c) Gel (liquid in solid)(iii) Mist and cloud
(d) Foam (gas in liquid)(iv) Cheese and jellies

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Colloidal systems are classified into eight types based on the physical states of the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Coloured glasses and gem stones consist of a solid dispersed in a solid, known as a solid sol, giving (a)-(ii). Mist, fog, and cloud consist of liquid droplets dispersed in a gas, known as an aerosol, giving (b)-(iii). Cheese and jellies consist of a liquid dispersed in a solid, known as a gel, giving (c)-(iv). Whipped cream, froth, and soap lather consist of a gas dispersed in a liquid, known as a foam, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - Matching enzymes with their biochemical reactions

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes in List I with the biochemical conversions they catalyse in List II:

List I (Enzyme)List II (Enzymatic reaction)
(a) Invertase(i) \(\text{Starch} \rightarrow \text{Maltose}\)
(b) Zymase(ii) \(\text{Sucrose} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Fructose}\)
(c) Diastase(iii) \(\text{Urea} \rightarrow \text{Ammonia} + \text{CO}_2\)
(d) Urease(iv) \(\text{Glucose} \rightarrow \text{Ethyl alcohol} + \text{CO}_2\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enzymes are highly specific biochemical catalysts; each enzyme catalyses a particular biochemical transformation.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Invertase (from yeast) catalyses the inversion of cane sugar (sucrose) into glucose and fructose, giving (a)-(ii). Zymase (from yeast) converts glucose into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide, giving (b)-(iv). Diastase (from malt) converts starch into maltose, giving (c)-(i). Urease (from soyabean) catalyses the decomposition of urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide, giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - Matching characteristics of physisorption and chemisorption

questiontext.text:
Match the adsorption features in List I with their corresponding quantitative or qualitative descriptions in List II:

List IList II
(a) Enthalpy of physisorption(i) Unimolecular layer
(b) Enthalpy of chemisorption(ii) \(20\text{--}40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(c) Layer formed in physisorption at high pressure(iii) \(80\text{--}240\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(d) Layer formed in chemisorption(iv) Multimolecular layers

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Physisorption arises from weak van der Waals' forces, whereas chemisorption involves strong covalent or ionic chemical bond formation.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Because van der Waals' interactions are weak, the enthalpy of physisorption is low (\(20\text{--}40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)), giving (a)-(ii). Chemisorption involves chemical bond formation, so its enthalpy is high (\(80\text{--}240\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)), giving (b)-(iii). Under high pressure, physisorption builds up multimolecular layers on the adsorbent surface, giving (c)-(iv). Chemisorption is limited to direct chemical bonding with surface atoms and therefore forms only a unimolecular layer, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - Matching adsorbents with their industrial and analytical applications

questiontext.text:
Match the adsorbent materials in List I with their specific applications in List II:

List IList II
(a) Activated charcoal in gas masks(i) Separation of a mixture of noble gases
(b) Silica and aluminium gels(ii) Adsorption of poisonous gases in coal mines
(c) Coconut charcoal at different temperatures(iii) Adsorption indicators at titration end points
(d) Silver halide precipitates with eosin or fluorescein(iv) Removal of moisture and control of humidity

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Adsorption finds widespread applications depending on the selectivity and surface properties of different adsorbents.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Gas masks contain activated charcoal or a mixture of adsorbents to adsorb poisonous gases for breathing in coal mines, giving (a)-(ii). Silica and aluminium gels are used as adsorbents to remove moisture and control humidity, giving (b)-(iv). A mixture of inert (noble) gases can be separated by differential adsorption on coconut charcoal at different temperatures, giving (c)-(i). Surfaces of silver halide precipitates adsorb dyes like eosin and fluorescein to produce a characteristic colour at the end point, acting as adsorption indicators, giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Matching industrial catalytic processes with catalysts

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial processes in List I with the catalysts used in List II:

List I (Process)List II (Catalyst)
(a) Haber's process for \(\mathrm{NH}_3\)(i) Platinised asbestos at \(573\text{ K}\)
(b) Ostwald's process for \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\)(ii) Vanadium pentoxide \(\left(\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5\right)\) at \(673\text{--}723\text{ K}\)
(c) Contact process for \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)(iii) Finely divided nickel
(d) Hydrogenation of vegetable oils(iv) Finely divided iron with molybdenum promoter

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial gaseous and liquid-phase reactions rely on specific solid heterogeneous catalysts to achieve practical reaction rates.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Haber's process for manufacturing ammonia uses finely divided iron with molybdenum as a promoter, giving (a)-(iv). Ostwald's process for nitric acid uses platinised asbestos at \(573\text{ K}\), giving (b)-(i). The Contact process for sulphuric acid uses platinised asbestos or \(\mathrm{V}_2\mathrm{O}_5\) at \(673\text{--}723\text{ K}\), giving (c)-(ii). Hydrogenation of vegetable oils uses finely divided nickel as the catalyst, giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - Matching catalyst selectivity for carbon monoxide and hydrogen

questiontext.text:
Match the catalysts in List I with the selective products formed from \(\mathrm{CO(g)}\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)}\) (or alcohols) in List II:

List I (Catalyst)List II (Reaction / Product)
(a) \(\mathrm{Ni}\)(i) \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OH(g)}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{Cu/ZnO{-}Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)(ii) \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4\mathrm{(g)} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O(g)}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{Cu}\)(iii) Alcohols \(\rightarrow\) Gasoline (petrol)
(d) \(\mathrm{ZSM{-}5}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{HCHO(g)}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Selectivity is the ability of a catalyst to direct a reaction to yield a particular product selectively when multiple products are possible from the same reactants.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
With \(\mathrm{Ni}\) as catalyst, \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)}\) yields \(\mathrm{CH}_4\mathrm{(g)} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O(g)}\), giving (a)-(ii). With \(\mathrm{Cu/ZnO{-}Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3\), \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)}\) yields \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OH(g)}\), giving (b)-(i). With \(\mathrm{Cu}\) alone, \(\mathrm{CO(g)} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{(g)}\) yields \(\mathrm{HCHO(g)}\), giving (c)-(iv). The zeolite catalyst \(\mathrm{ZSM{-}5}\) converts alcohols directly into gasoline by dehydration, giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - Matching colloidal types with examples and properties

questiontext.text:
Match the colloidal categories in List I with their characteristic examples or descriptions in List II:

List IList II
(a) Lyophilic colloid(i) Aggregates of \(\mathrm{S}_8\) molecules
(b) Lyophobic colloid(ii) Starch, cellulose, and polythene
(c) Multimolecular colloid(iii) Reversible sol formed by gum or gelatine
(d) Macromolecular colloid(iv) Irreversible sol of metallic sulphides

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Colloids are classified both by dispersed phase–medium interaction (lyophilic vs lyophobic) and by particle type (multimolecular, macromolecular, and associated).

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Lyophilic colloids such as gum and gelatine form reversible sols directly upon mixing, giving (a)-(iii). Lyophobic colloids such as metals and metallic sulphides are irreversible sols, giving (b)-(iv). Multimolecular colloids consist of aggregates of many smaller atoms or molecules, such as a sulphur sol containing \(\mathrm{S}_8\) molecules, giving (c)-(i). Macromolecular colloids consist of single giant molecules (natural or synthetic polymers like starch, cellulose, and polythene) of colloidal size, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q09 - Matching chemical reactions used in sol preparation

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical reactions for preparing colloidal sols in List I with the corresponding reaction types in List II:

List I (Reaction)List II (Reaction type)
(a) \(\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3(\text{sol}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(i) Reduction
(b) \(\mathrm{SO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{S}(\text{sol}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(ii) Hydrolysis
(c) \(2\mathrm{AuCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{HCHO} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Au}(\text{sol}) + 3\mathrm{HCOOH} + 6\mathrm{HCl}\)(iii) Double decomposition
(d) \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe(OH)}_3(\text{sol}) + 3\mathrm{HCl}\)(iv) Oxidation

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Colloidal dispersions can be prepared by chemical reactions such as double decomposition, oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis, followed by aggregation of the formed molecules into colloidal size.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
The reaction \(\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3(\text{sol}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is a double decomposition reaction, giving (a)-(iii). The reaction \(\mathrm{SO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{S}(\text{sol}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) involves oxidation of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}\) to sulphur sol, giving (b)-(iv). The reaction of \(\mathrm{AuCl}_3\) with formaldehyde (\(\mathrm{HCHO}\)) reduces \(\mathrm{Au}^{3+}\) to metallic \(\mathrm{Au}(\text{sol})\), giving (c)-(i). The reaction of \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) with hot water is a hydrolysis reaction yielding \(\mathrm{Fe(OH)}_3(\text{sol})\), giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q10 - Matching purification and dispersion techniques for colloids

questiontext.text:
Match the colloidal techniques in List I with their correct descriptions in List II:

List I (Technique)List II (Description)
(a) Dialysis(i) Converting a precipitate into a sol using a small amount of electrolyte
(b) Electro-dialysis(ii) Separating sol particles using filter paper impregnated with collodion
(c) Ultrafiltration(iii) Removing dissolved substances by diffusion through parchment paper
(d) Peptization(iv) Accelerating electrolyte removal from a sol using an electric field

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Colloidal solutions are prepared by methods like peptization and purified by dialysis, electro-dialysis, or ultrafiltration.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Dialysis removes dissolved crystalloids by diffusion through an animal membrane or parchment paper, giving (a)-(iii). Electro-dialysis speeds up dialysis by applying an electric field when the impurity is an electrolyte, giving (b)-(iv). Ultrafiltration uses filter paper impregnated with collodion (\(4\%\) nitrocellulose in alcohol-ether) and hardened with formaldehyde to retain colloidal particles, giving (c)-(ii). Peptization converts a freshly prepared precipitate into a colloidal sol by shaking with dispersion medium and a small amount of electrolyte (peptizing agent), giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q11 - Matching common colloidal sols with their electric charge

questiontext.text:
Match the colloidal sols in List I with their classification by electric charge in List II:

List I (Sol)List II (Nature and charge)
(a) \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(i) Negatively charged metallic sulphide sol
(b) \(\mathrm{CdS}\)(ii) Positively charged hydrated metallic oxide sol
(c) Haemoglobin (blood)(iii) Negatively charged acid dye sol
(d) Congo red(iv) Positively charged biological sol

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
All particles in a given colloidal sol carry the same sign of electric charge—either positive or negative.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Hydrated metallic oxides such as \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) are positively charged sols, giving (a)-(ii). Metallic sulphides such as \(\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3\) and \(\mathrm{CdS}\) are negatively charged sols, giving (b)-(i). Haemoglobin (blood) is a positively charged sol, giving (c)-(iv). Acid dye stuffs such as eosin and congo red form negatively charged sols (whereas basic dyes like methylene blue are positively charged), giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q12 - Matching Freundlich isotherm parameters and limiting cases

questiontext.text:
Match the Freundlich adsorption isotherm conditions or parameters in List I with their corresponding physical interpretations in List II:

List IList II
(a) \(\frac{1}{n} = 0\)(i) \(\frac{x}{m} \propto p\) (adsorption varies directly with pressure)
(b) \(\frac{1}{n} = 1\)(ii) Slope of \(\log\frac{x}{m}\) vs \(\log p\) straight line
(c) \(\frac{1}{n}\) in \(\log\frac{x}{m} = \log k + \frac{1}{n}\log p\)(iii) \(\frac{x}{m} = \text{constant}\) (independent of pressure)
(d) \(\log k\) in \(\log\frac{x}{m} = \log k + \frac{1}{n}\log p\)(iv) Intercept on the \(\log\frac{x}{m}\) axis

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Freundlich adsorption isotherm is \(\frac{x}{m} = k \cdot p^{1/n}\), which in logarithmic form is \(\log\frac{x}{m} = \log k + \frac{1}{n}\log p\).

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
When \(\frac{1}{n} = 0\), \(p^0 = 1\), so \(\frac{x}{m} = k = \text{constant}\), meaning adsorption is independent of pressure, giving (a)-(iii). When \(\frac{1}{n} = 1\), \(\frac{x}{m} = kp\), so \(\frac{x}{m} \propto p\) (adsorption varies directly with pressure), giving (b)-(i). Comparing \(\log\frac{x}{m} = \log k + \frac{1}{n}\log p\) with \(y = c + mx\), the coefficient \(\frac{1}{n}\) is the slope of the straight line, giving (c)-(ii), and \(\log k\) is the y-intercept on the \(\log\frac{x}{m}\) axis, giving (d)-(iv).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q13 - Matching preferential adsorption conditions with sol charge

questiontext.text:
Match the preparation conditions in List I with the resulting charged colloidal sol in List II:

List I (Mixing condition)List II (Resulting sol)
(a) Dilute \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) added to excess dilute \(\mathrm{KI}\)(i) \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) (positively charged)
(b) Dilute \(\mathrm{KI}\) added to excess dilute \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\)(ii) \(\mathrm{AgI}/\mathrm{I}^-\) (negatively charged)
(c) \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) added to excess hot water(iii) \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{OH}^-\) (negatively charged)
(d) \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) added to \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution(iv) \(\mathrm{AgI}/\mathrm{Ag}^+\) (positively charged)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sol particles acquire positive or negative charge by preferential adsorption of the common ion present in excess in the dispersion medium.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
When \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) is added to excess \(\mathrm{KI}\), \(\mathrm{I}^-\) ions are in excess and are adsorbed on \(\mathrm{AgI}\), forming negatively charged \(\mathrm{AgI}/\mathrm{I}^-\), giving (a)-(ii). When \(\mathrm{KI}\) is added to excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\), \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) ions are adsorbed on \(\mathrm{AgI}\), forming positively charged \(\mathrm{AgI}/\mathrm{Ag}^+\), giving (b)-(iv). Adding \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) to excess hot water yields positively charged \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) due to \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) adsorption, giving (c)-(i). Adding \(\mathrm{FeCl}_3\) to \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution produces negatively charged \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{OH}^-\) due to \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) adsorption, giving (d)-(iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q14 - Matching colloidal properties with their underlying mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match the colloidal phenomena in List I with their governing causes or definitions in List II:

List I (Phenomenon)List II (Cause / Definition)
(a) Tyndall effect(i) Unbalanced bombardment of sol particles by dispersion medium molecules
(b) Brownian movement(ii) Movement of dispersion medium in an electric field when sol particles cannot move
(c) Electrophoresis(iii) Scattering of light by colloidal particles in all directions
(d) Electroosmosis(iv) Movement of charged colloidal particles toward oppositely charged electrodes

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Colloidal solutions exhibit characteristic optical, kinetic, and electrokinetic properties due to particle size and surface charge.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Tyndall effect is the illumination of a light beam's path caused by scattering of light by colloidal particles in all directions, giving (a)-(iii). Brownian movement is the continuous zig-zag motion caused by unbalanced bombardment of colloidal particles by molecules of the dispersion medium, giving (b)-(i). Electrophoresis is the migration of charged colloidal particles under an applied electric potential, giving (c)-(iv). Electroosmosis is the movement of the dispersion medium in an electric field when the movement of colloidal particles is prevented, giving (d)-(ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q15 - Matching coagulation concepts and Hardy-Schulze rule

questiontext.text:
Match the coagulation terms or processes in List I with their correct descriptions in List II:

List IList II
(a) Mutual coagulation(i) \(\mathrm{Al}^{3+} > \mathrm{Ba}^{2+} > \mathrm{Na}^{+}\)
(b) Persistent dialysis(ii) Minimum concentration in \(\text{mmol L}^{-1}\) needed for precipitation in \(2\text{ h}\)
(c) Coagulating value(iii) Mixing hydrated ferric oxide and arsenious sulphide sols
(d) Flocculating power for a negative sol(iv) Complete removal of stabilising electrolyte traces

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lyophobic sols are stabilised by surface charge and traces of electrolytes; neutralising or removing this charge leads to coagulation.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
Mixing oppositely charged sols such as positively charged hydrated ferric oxide and negatively charged arsenious sulphide in nearly equal proportions causes mutual coagulation, giving (a)-(iii). Prolonged (persistent) dialysis removes almost all traces of stabilising electrolytes, causing the colloid to coagulate, giving (b)-(iv). Coagulating value is defined as the minimum concentration of an electrolyte in millimoles per litre required to cause precipitation of a sol in two hours, giving (c)-(ii). By the Hardy-Schulze rule, higher-valence cations have greater flocculating power for a negative sol: \(\mathrm{Al}^{3+} > \mathrm{Ba}^{2+} > \mathrm{Na}^{+}\), giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SURFACECHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q16 - Matching emulsifiers and natural colloidal applications

questiontext.text:
Match the colloidal systems or applications in List I with their corresponding agents or mechanisms in List II:

List IList II
(a) Principal emulsifying agents for \(\text{O/W}\) emulsions(i) Mutual coagulation of positively charged hide and negatively charged tannin
(b) Principal emulsifying agents for \(\text{W/O}\) emulsions(ii) Coagulation of colloidal clay in river water by sea water electrolytes
(c) Formation of delta(iii) Proteins, gums, natural and synthetic soaps
(d) Tanning of leather(iv) Heavy metal salts of fatty acids, long chain alcohols, lampblack

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Emulsions are stabilised by specific emulsifying agents depending on the dispersion medium, and many natural or industrial processes rely on coagulation of colloids.

Step 2: Matching Each Pair
For oil-in-water (\(\text{O/W}\)) emulsions, the principal emulsifying agents are proteins, gums, and natural or synthetic soaps, giving (a)-(iii). For water-in-oil (\(\text{W/O}\)) emulsions, they are heavy metal salts of fatty acids, long chain alcohols, and lampblack, giving (b)-(iv). Deltas form where river water (a colloidal solution of clay) meets sea water, whose electrolytes coagulate the clay, giving (c)-(ii). Tanning occurs when positively charged animal hides are soaked in negatively charged tannin, causing mutual coagulation and hardening of leather, giving (d)-(i).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).
